name: The Square household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: square_geo

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 April 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-04-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-04-01 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.name: Geo. Square

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print '3. Geo. Square t 3 first rate' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 April 1834, column 2 — dated 1834-04-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.summary: Geo. Square may be a transcription/duplicate relation to George Squire; Joliet is competing geography, so both resident IDs and the candidate relation are preserved.

merge_ruling.for_merge: “Geo.” is the ordinary abbreviation of “George”, Square and Squire differ by one letter, and the resident layer holds one card of each and no other bearer of either stem. Pass 06 of the resident-research programme reached the pair and wrote it down as a possible duplicate: “Geo. Square may be a transcription/duplicate relation to George Squire”.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE QUESTION CANNOT BE ASKED YET, BECAUSE ONE OF THE TWO PRINTED LINES IS ITSELF CONTESTED — and this corpus contests it in its own committed words. `square_geo` is minted from the Democrat of 1 April 1834, whose line reads “3. Geo. Square t 3 first rate”: an S-run line with an advertisement's column bleeding through it. The extraction of the 16 April 1834 impression — which that file's own note calls “the best witness to the J-W half of the 1 April 1834 list that the corpus holds” — reads the SAME three consecutive lines as “Benjarnin Smith”, “Ira Saymoro” and “GEO. SAVER” where 1 April reads “Benjamin Reed”, “Ira Raymore” and “Geo. Square”, and records that “the alphabetical position is with this printing and against 1834-04-01's” while declining to rewrite a minted name on a second transcription of equal rank. So the town does not yet know whether it holds a Square at all. A merge cannot be tested against a line nobody has settled — R5's principle, moved from a garbled forename to a garbled surname — and a REFUSAL cannot honestly be entered either, because the refusal would rest on the same unread line. Neither D6 nor C9 is reached for: both ask what the returns print, and one of these two returns has two readings.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
